title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 697–699): U_{0,3} = P^1 − {0,1,∞} over Q with its S_3 symmetry. 𝓜_{0,3} = π1(U_{0,3,Q}, S_3; j̄) is the fundamental group of the quotient stack [U_{0,3}/S_3], i.e. the λ-line modulo S_3, essentially the j-line. It sits in an exact sequence 1 → π̂_{0,3} → 𝓜_{0,3} → Γ_Q × S_3 → 1 (eq. 240 on the next page). The abelianization of π̂_{0,3} is M̂, which as a Galois module is roughly (Ẑ^3/diag)(1) or the sum-zero sublattice, Tate-twisted. The action of Γ_Q × S_3 on M̂ factors through χ × id : Γ_Q × S_3 → Ẑ^* × S_3, where χ is the cyclotomic character. Aff = (Ẑ^* × S_3) ⋉ M̂ is the corresponding affine group (235/237).

This page states the following. The 'structure (230)' is the abelianized extension 𝓜_1 = 𝓜_{0,3}/[π̂, π̂] of Γ_Q × S_3 by M̂. Up to non-unique isomorphism, giving it is the same as giving an M̂-conjugacy class of lifts 𝓜_{0,3} → Aff of the map 𝓜_{0,3} → Ẑ^* × S_3 (238). The margin adds that the characteristic property of such a lift is that its restriction to π̂_{0,3} is the canonical map π̂_{0,3} → (π̂_{0,3})^{ab} ≅ M̂. In modern terms, such a lift identifies 𝓜_1 with the pullback of the split extension Aff. So it exists exactly when the abelianized extension splits. The previous page first claims non-splitting, then corrects itself ('si, elle est triviale'). A concrete lift comes from choosing an origin point ȳ in U_{0,3}(Q̄), or a tangential point. Moving the origin changes the lift by an inner automorphism by some x in M̂, so only the M̂-conjugacy class is canonical.

Grothendieck then observes that the maximal abelian pro-cover of P^1 − {0,1,∞} is the Fermat tower (the curves x^n + y^n = 1). So this conjugacy class of lifts is exactly what the Fermat tower, with its Γ_Q and S_3 actions, gives. Its knowledge is 'in principle equivalent' to knowing the Fermat tower up to isomorphism.

He proposes to relate these lifts to the earlier homomorphisms (217)/(218). (218) gives a canonical homomorphism of 𝓜_{0,3}, not into Aff but into an analogous group G_{ρ,σ}/μ (232). Here G_{ρ,σ} is plausibly the profinite group generated by elements ρ of order 3 and σ of order 2, i.e. the completion of PSL_2(Z) = Z/3 * Z/2, the orbifold π1 of the j-line, divided by a central or cyclotomic piece μ. This homomorphism also lifts 𝓜_{0,3} → Ẑ^* × S_3. The next page builds the comparison diagram (239)–(241) and passes to the metabelian-style quotient 𝓜_1.

Purpose: to understand the abelian (Fermat / Kummer, and ultimately Jacobi-sum) layer of the Galois action on π̂_1(P^1 − 3 points) equivariantly for S_3, as a first step of the Longue Marche programme.
errors: The previous page first asserts that the extension of S_3 by M̂ is non-trivial, then corrects this in an insertion ('si, elle est triviale'). This page implicitly uses the corrected statement: a lift to Aff exists only because the abelianized extension splits.

The claim that the class of lifts 'équivaut en principe' to the Fermat tower up to isomorphism is heuristic. The lift encodes the tower only as a pro-cover with Galois and S_3 action, i.e. as a split abelian extension. All arithmetically interesting data (Jacobi sums) sit at the next, metabelian level, which this page does not reach.

ideas.what: S_3-equivariant arithmetic fundamental group of P^1−{0,1,∞}, i.e. π1 of the stack quotient [U_{0,3}/S_3] (the j-line), as an extension of Γ_Q × S_3
ideas.modern_name: orbifold/stack fundamental group of M_{0,4}/S_4, related to M_{1,1}; GT-type symmetries
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse); Drinfeld, Ihara, Nakamura for GT and its relations
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (discussion of M_{0,4}, M_{1,1} and the Teichmüller tower); La Longue Marche

ideas.what: The abelianized extension corresponds to M̂-conjugacy classes of lifts into the affine group (Ẑ^* × S_3) ⋉ M̂; base-point change acts by translation/inner automorphism
ideas.modern_name: splitting of the abelianized fundamental exact sequence; Kummer theory / H^1 torsor of sections
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (Grothendieck SGA1 formalism; Deligne 1989 on tangential base points)

ideas.what: The maximal abelian pro-cover of P^1−{0,1,∞} is the Fermat tower, so the abelianized Galois/S_3 data equal the Fermat tower structure
ideas.modern_name: Fermat tower as abelian cover of P^1 minus three points

ideas.what: Comparing the lift to Aff with a canonical homomorphism (218) into G_{ρ,σ}/μ, the analogue built from the (ρ,σ) presentation, PSL_2-like
ideas.modern_name: relation between the abelianized Galois action and the action via profinite PSL_2(Z)/GT

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes to systematically match the abelian lifts 𝓜_{0,3} → Aff (Fermat tower data) with the canonical homomorphism (218) into the PSL_2-type group G_{ρ,σ}/μ, S_3-equivariantly. The page leaves this as a programme.
missed.quote: Cela conduirait à mettre, si possible, ces relèvements en correspondance avec les homom. (217), et plus particulièrement sans doute avec (218)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The S_3-equivariant (j-line) treatment of the Fermat/Jacobi-sum layer is less standard than Ihara's non-equivariant one. It is mildly relevant to GT-symmetry questions, but likely subsumed by work of Ihara, Anderson and Nakamura.

deep.surprise_reason: The page carries out a standard reformulation: the abelianized extension as conjugacy classes of lifts into an affine group, plus the identification of the abelian tower with the Fermat tower. Both are known (Ihara, Anderson, Deligne). The only less-common element is the S_3/j-line-equivariant viewpoint, and the proposed link to the canonical map into G_{ρ,σ}/μ is only sketched.
transcription_corrections: 'Ĝ_3' should be 𝔖_3, the symmetric group: 'M_{0,3} → 𝔖_3 × Ẑ^*'.
'M_{0,3}' throughout is script 𝓜_{0,3}, the group π1(U_{0,3,Q}, 𝔖_3; j̄), not the moduli space.
'U_∞(Q̄)' is likely 'U_{0,3}(Q̄)'; the point written 'ȳ' may be j̄ (the base point).
'G_{p,0}/μ_a' should read 'G_{ρ,σ}/μ_G', as in (239) on the next page.
Margin: 'NB Cet homom. induit sur π̂_{0,3} l'homom. canonique π̂_{0,3} → (π̂_{0,3})_{ab} ≅ M̂ ; propriété caractéristique de (238)'.
